clue.text: Rush about with bottle-opener and drink

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of rush are turned around into a new order
the opener of the bottle is the letter it starts with

explanation.surface: Someone dashes around with a corkscrew and something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges RUSH to SHRU; the 'opener' of 'bottle' adds B. A shrub is an old drink of fruit juice and spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub is an old-fashioned cordial of fruit juice, sugar and rum or brandy.

clue.text: Occasionally moulds seem moist

indicators.note: moulds is a verb here: shapes the letters of seem moist into a fresh form

explanation.surface: Damp conditions sometimes produce mould.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moulds' looks like the fungus but is the verb 'shapes', rearranging SEEM MOIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something occasionally means doing it now and then, not always.

clue.text: Row involving cattle-grazing

explanation.surface: A dispute about where the herds may graze.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a row of mountains or items, and also open land where cattle graze.

clue.text: The money that's about may be used for underwear

parts.note: brass is slang for money
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for 'that is'
re is Latin-derived 'concerning', i.e. about

explanation.surface: The cash lying around might go on lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' stands for 'that is', abbreviated IE; 'about' is RE as in business letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassiere is a bra, an item of women's undergarments.

clue.text: Keeps going for brochures

parts.note: pro is Latin for 'for', as in pros and cons
tracts are short pamphlets

explanation.surface: Someone holds on to the leaflets.
explanation.definitionFit: To protract is to prolong or extend something in time.

clue.text: His work output is impressive!

parts.note: a ... output is literally impressed, ink pressed onto paper, so 'impressive' is a pun

explanation.surface: Praise for a productive worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A printer produces impressions, pages pressed with ink, so the work is literally impressive.

clue.text: Go too high and there's nothing green and nothing soft

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
vert is the heraldic word for green
nothing again gives the letter O
p is piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: An overreaching climber has no grass and no softness.
explanation.walkthrough: VERT is green in heraldry; P (piano) means soft in music.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtop is to rise above or exceed a limit.

clue.text: Its speakers arrive by air

parts.note: the voices heard on this set are carried over the airwaves, not by plane

explanation.surface: Visitors landing by aeroplane.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasts reach a receiver through the airwaves, so the voices in a wireless set come over the air.

clue.text: Temperate land mass

explanation.surface: A description of a mild part of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Continent means self-restrained or moderate, and also one of the earth's great land masses.

clue.text: Caught a whiff of fish

explanation.surface: Someone noticed a fishy smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Smelt is a past tense of smell, and the smelt is a small silvery food fish.

clue.text: A fighting man holds with juicy fruit

indicators.note: holds signals that one word is held within another

parts.note: a marine is a soldier serving on ships
and means together with

explanation.surface: A soldier grips a juicy piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts AND inside MARINE, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandarine, or mandarin, is a small, sweet citrus fruit like a tangerine.

clue.text: Studies English, being stupid

parts.note: dens are private studies, rooms for working

explanation.surface: Someone studies English but proves slow-witted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Studies' looks like a verb but is the noun: rooms, dens.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense is a colloquial word for slow-witted.

clue.text: Actress ignoring bill for hair

indicators.note: ignoring tells us to leave some letters of actress out

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A performer pays no attention to the invoice for her hairdo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' removes AC (account, a bill) from ACTRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a lock or long strand of hair.

clue.text: He'll have designs on any who patronise him

definitions.text: He'll have designs on any who patronise him

parts.words: He'll have designs on any who patronise him
parts.note: 'have designs on' sounds like scheming, but literally he draws designs on to his customers' skin

explanation.surface: A schemer who exploits his customers.
explanation.definitionFit: An ink artist puts pictures permanently on the skin of each client.

clue.text: 19 dn could be such a manipulator!

indicators.note: could be signals the letters of the 19 down answer may be made into something else

parts.note: the answer to 19 down, the Dutch scholar

explanation.surface: A scholar who might turn out to be a manipulator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges ERASMUS, the 19 down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur kneads and works the muscles by hand.

clue.text: Nice teens fashion awareness

indicators.note: fashion is a verb here, to shape the letters of nice teens anew

explanation.surface: Pleasant teenagers shape consciousness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' looks like a noun but is the verb 'shape', rearranging NICE TEENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentience is the capacity to feel and perceive, consciousness.

clue.text: A ship the lawmen go ahead and occupy

indicators.note: go ahead puts the lawmen in front of the ship

parts.note: a posse is a band of men summoned by a sheriff
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: Sheriff's men advance and take over a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess is to own or hold, as in taking occupation of territory.

clue.text: Directions on bridging, leaving no loopholes

parts.note: S and E are south and east, compass directions
arching means spanning, as a bridge does

explanation.surface: Instructions about bridge building that cover every gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A searching inquiry is thorough and probing, missing nothing.

clue.text: Withdrew, a little hurt

explanation.surface: Someone pulled out, slightly injured.
explanation.definitionFit: Scratched means pulled out of a race, and also grazed or slightly wounded.

clue.text: Frank seeing that soldiers join up

parts.note: since means because, seeing that
RE is the Royal Engineers, British Army soldiers

explanation.surface: Frank notes that the troops are enlisting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name but is the adjective. RE is the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank means honest and open, genuine.

clue.text: A scholar, given time, adds up

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word sums is read from bottom to top

parts.note: sums means adds

explanation.surface: Given time, an academic works out totals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SUMS to SMUS in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus was the Dutch humanist, one of the great Renaissance thinkers.

clue.text: Broadcast parts of TT races

indicators.note: parts of suggests the letters of TT races are split up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Coverage of sections of the Isle of Man motorcycle races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' suggests radio, but means strewn. The TT races are motorcycle races on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast seed is to sow it widely, spreading it about.

clue.text: "Pains of love be far than all other pleasures are." (Dryden)

definitions.text: "Pains of love be far than all other pleasures are." (Dryden)

parts.words: "Pains of love be far than all other pleasures are." (Dryden)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing comparative completes Dryden's line from Tyrannic Love

explanation.surface: A line of Dryden's verse on the delights of love.
explanation.definitionFit: Dryden's song says love's pains are more pleasant than every other pleasure.

clue.text: Neat figure — with the hips under restraint!

indicators.note: under restraint means held in, so one word is enclosed by another

parts.note: shape means figure or form

explanation.surface: A trim figure achieved by a corset holding in the hips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under restraint' puts HIPS inside SHAPE, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipshape means tidy and in good order, as on a well-run ship.

clue.text: Portly porter

explanation.surface: A fat doorman.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout means fat, and stout is also a strong dark beer like porter.

clue.text: Control the beast!

explanation.surface: An urgent plea to restrain an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer is to guide or direct, and a steer is a young castrated bull.

clue.text: Approach a junction. There's a long tailback

parts.note: come means approach
a T-junction, shaped like the letter T

explanation.surface: A driver nears a junction and meets a long traffic queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailback' looks like a traffic jam, but the definition is a body with a long tail behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet is a celestial body trailing a long glowing tail behind it.

clue.text: A girl will take many a look back

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, many

indicators.note: back means the word air is turned to read the other way

parts.note: air means a look or appearance

explanation.surface: Someone will look back at many a passing woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns AIR to RIA. M is the Roman thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Light-weight animal

explanation.surface: A small creature that weighs little.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a small unit of weight, and also the snow leopard.

clue.text: Demonstration about courts that lack a dominant woman

indicators.note: about means one word goes round another

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration

indicators.note: lack tells us the courts go without the single letter named next

parts.note: atria are open courts, the plural of atrium
taken as written

explanation.surface: A protest about courtyards lacking a female ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lack a' drops an A from ATRIA (plural of atrium, open courts), leaving ATRI; 'about' puts MARCH round that, after its M.
explanation.definitionFit: A matriarch is a woman who rules a family or group.

clue.text: A speculator sees the upswing in gold

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in means the upswing sits inside the word for gold

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
rise means an upswing

explanation.surface: A gambler watches gold prices climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts RISE inside OR, heraldic gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A theoriser speculates, forming ideas without proof.

clue.text: A king, and so majestic

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: A king, and therefore majestic.
explanation.walkthrough: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George, as on British postboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand means splendid and imposing.
